Reconcile every Stripe webhook endpoint's enabled_events with what subscription-webhook actually handles
An event Stripe never sends is dead code that reads as working — no error, no log; CI and code review cannot see Stripe-side config
Runs INSIDE Supabase so the four account/mode Stripe secrets never leave the function environment and no operator holds them
Additive only — never removes an event added by hand for a reason this repo does not know about
POST {} previews the diff; only {"apply": true} writes to Stripe
Auth accepts the service-role key OR a super admin, so the reconciler can be driven from inside the database
Sweeps the uk/uae x test/live matrix; a key not configured for a combination is a skip, not an error
An endpoint already subscribed to '*' is left untouched
Hourly pg_cron sweep that runs Tesla Supercharger sync for every tenant with the integration enabled
One tenant's sync failure is caught and reported per-tenant instead of aborting the whole sweep
User-initiated Supercharger sync behind the portal refresh button
A requested tenantId that is not the caller's own is rejected unless the caller is a super admin
Refuses to sync unless tenants.integration_tesla_fleet is true
Optional rentalId/vehicleId narrows a manual sync to one booking; the cron path always syncs the whole fleet
Tesla Fleet API tenant integration console: connect, disconnect, status, VIN compatibility, vehicle listing
The same function serves Tesla's OAuth redirect over GET, so one generic redirect_uri works for every tenant
HMAC-signed state is the gate that stops an attacker forging a callback that points at another tenant
Single cross-tenant guard helper applied to every authenticated action
VIN check against the tenant's Tesla account flips vehicles.tesla_fleet_enabled and stores the Tesla vehicle id
Disconnect clears the Vault tokens and resets tesla_fleet_enabled/vehicle_id on every vehicle of the tenant
Storing tokens is an RPC that also flips tenants.integration_tesla_fleet to true — connection state is a side effect of token storage
returnUrl is carried inside the signed state and the callback redirects back with ?tesla_connected=true
Trax's plain-English 'why this price' narrative for a pricing suggestion
public.trax_price_suggest RPC — the deterministic pricing math whose breakdown this function narrates
The math already decided the number; the model may only paraphrase a deterministic fact sheet and never invent figures
confidence 'none' returns canned copy without ever calling OpenAI
If the model returns nothing, a templated sentence is built from the same comps/median facts
Voice contract: first name once, 2-3 sentences, plain prose, acknowledge a small comparable set when confidence is low
Explanation is grounded in cross-tenant network comparables (p25/median/p75) plus the vehicle's own 90-day utilisation
Inbound SMS lands in the tenant's unified customer chat thread
Tenant is identified by matching the To number against tenants.twilio_phone_number, retried with/without the leading '+'
Customer resolution: exact phone match, then a full-table scan matching on digit-suffix
Get-or-create a chat_channels row per (tenant, customer) so an inbound SMS never has nowhere to land
Messages from unrecognised numbers are kept in sms_unknown_threads rather than dropped
Always answers Twilio with an empty 200 TwiML, even on internal failure, so Twilio does not retry or mark the number broken
Each inbound message stamps chat_channels.last_message_at/last_channel so the omnichannel inbox can sort and label threads
Twilio MessageSid is stored as external_id — the join key the delivery-status webhook later updates against
Inbound WhatsApp lands in the same unified customer chat thread, tagged channel='whatsapp'
Twilio's 'whatsapp:' address prefix is stripped from both From and To before any matching
Tenant resolved against tenants.twilio_whatsapp_number, a column distinct from the SMS number
The same exact-then-suffix customer phone resolution as the SMS webhook, re-implemented inline
Unknown WhatsApp senders are stored in sms_unknown_threads — the SMS-named tables carry both channels
Twilio delivery receipts update the stored message's external_status across both known and unknown threads
Update chat_channel_messages first; if no row matched, try sms_unknown_messages — the same SID can live in either table
Every callback is archived into sms_message_log with error_code, error_message and the full raw form payload
Always returns 200 to Twilio, even on internal error, to stop callback retries
Outbound click-to-call: TwiML that dials the customer from the browser softphone using the tenant's caller ID
Tenant is identified by the Twilio AccountSid on the request — the BYO-Twilio identity of the caller
Browser client identity is encoded as 'client:tenant_{app_user_id}', decoded back into call_logs.caller_id
Dialled number resolved to a customer by exact then digit-suffix matching (third copy of the same routine)
When call_recording_enabled, a spoken consent line precedes the Dial and record-from-answer posts to process-call-recording
A failed call_logs insert is logged but never fails the call — telephony beats bookkeeping
Inbound customer call rings every active staff browser client and their forwarding phones simultaneously
Only a tenant whose number matches AND has twilio_voice_enabled will accept the call
Caller resolved to a customer by exact then digit-suffix matching (fourth copy of the same routine)
Super admins (tenant_id NULL) are added to the ring group alongside the tenant's own staff
Forwarding numbers that resolve to the Twilio number itself are dropped to prevent a call loop
forwarding_caller_id_mode='business_line' makes staff phones show the business line so they know it is a work call
Business-line mode hides the customer's number, so a whisper leg is attached to speak the caller's name before bridging
answerOnBridge is added only when the whisper is active, so the customer hears ringback instead of dead air during the announcement
The 30s Dial action hands off to twilio-voicemail-handler carrying tenantId, callSid, from, to, customerId and channelId in the query string
Preview=1 renders the exact TwiML the dev panel would produce without logging a call or ringing anyone
With no active users at all, the call goes straight to voicemail if enabled, otherwise a spoken apology
Voice status callbacks drive the call_logs state machine and stamp ended_at on terminal statuses
A completed call is written into the conversation thread as a channel='voice' message with duration metadata
An all-zero UUID stands in for an unknown sender because chat_channel_messages.sender_id cannot be null
If no call_logs row exists for the SID, a minimal one is synthesised from AccountSid with admittedly guessed caller_type and direction
Whisper leg that announces the caller's name to the staff member only, then bridges the two parties
No press-a-key screening: a Gather+Hangup makes Twilio report DialCallStatus=completed, indistinguishable from an answered call, which would dead-end the customer past the voicemail handler
Safe screening requires a per-call 'screened-declined' marker shared with the voicemail handler — a schema change not yet made
CNAM caller-name display is US-only, so a spoken announcement is the only carrier-independent way to convey a name on UK phones
On error the whisper returns empty TwiML and connects the call rather than dropping it
test=1 renders a standalone dev-panel confirmation call that announces and hangs up because there is no bridge target
Caller names are XML-escaped before entering the TwiML document
Two-phase voicemail: the Dial action plays the greeting and records, the Record action persists the recording
DialCallStatus 'completed'/'answered' is treated as answered, so no voicemail is offered — the exact assumption the whisper's no-screening note protects
The Twilio mp3 is fetched with the tenant's own Twilio basic auth and re-hosted in the 'voicemails' bucket so a browser can play it without Twilio credentials
If the re-host fails the Twilio URL is stored as-is rather than losing the voicemail
The voicemail row is back-linked to its call_logs row via twilio_call_sid after insert
A voicemail also appears in the customer thread as a channel='voice' message carrying the recording URL in metadata
Greeting is the tenant's uploaded voicemail_greeting_url, falling back to a spoken company-name message
Undo a manually recorded payment for one rental+category: unwind allocations, restore charge remaining_amount, delete P&L rows
Refuses the undo when any Refund ledger entry exists for that category — the operator must use Refund instead
Only payments with no stripe_payment_intent_id, not Reversed and not refunding, may be undone — card money is never unwound by hand
P&L rows are located by the composite source_ref '{paymentId}_{chargeId}' — an undocumented naming contract with whatever wrote them
A payment with no allocations left is deleted outright; one with allocations elsewhere has remaining_amount and Partial/Credit/Applied status recomputed
The rental is read through the caller's own RLS-scoped client to prove access, then every mutation runs as service role
The unwind is a sequence of independent statements that 'continue' on failure — a mid-way error leaves the ledger partially reverted with no rollback
Replace a manager's per-tab access grants in one privileged call
A hardcoded ALLOWED_TAB_KEYS whitelist duplicating apps/portal/src/lib/permissions.ts — a new portal tab must be added in both places or it silently 400s
Only an active head_admin (or a super admin) may write grants, and only for a manager in their own tenant
The target user's role must literally be 'manager' — granular grants exist for no other role
Grants are deleted then re-inserted without a transaction: a failed insert leaves the manager with zero permissions
An empty permission array is rejected so a manager can never be saved with no access at all
Every grant change is recorded in audit_logs with the target email and the full permission set
Card-on-file rotation for installment plans via a Stripe SetupIntent (create-setup / confirm / get-card)
A stored stripe_customer_id is validated before reuse because Stripe customers are scoped per account+mode and a test-era id fails with 'No such customer'
SetupIntent uses usage:'off_session' because the saved card is charged unattended for future installments
The payment method must already belong to this Stripe customer before it is made the default
With no plan id supplied, the new card is written onto every active/overdue installment plan for the customer
The tenant -> Stripe account/mode/Connect-options resolution block is copy-pasted four times in this one file
Phone-side validation of the QR token that hands a desktop-started AI identity verification to the customer's phone
Distinct 410 (expired) and 409 (already completed) answers so the phone page can explain what to do next
Returns the tenant's slug, company name and logo so the phone capture page is branded as the operator, not Drive247
Returns session_id (falling back to the row id) explicitly 'for consistency with desktop' — this is the key both devices poll on
Scanning the QR flips the verification row to pending/pending, which is how the desktop learns the phone picked it up
Validation does not revoke or rotate the QR token, so the same code stays usable until its expiry
Unauthenticated resolution of a customer registration invite token into tenant branding and form configuration
An expired invite is flipped to status 'expired' on read — expiry is enforced lazily, with no cron
Only a 'pending' invite resolves; used or revoked links are refused with the same generic message
Returns the tenant's accepted_verification_document (defaulting to drivers_license) so the registration form knows which document to demand
Re-check user-edited identity fields against the document image with GPT-4o vision before accepting the edit
approved=true only if every supplied field matches — one mismatch fails the whole edit
A field that cannot be read off the document returns documentValue null and matches=true — unreadable is not a mismatch
Names and country codes are matched loosely; dates and document numbers must match exactly
Supabase public storage URLs are pulled through the storage API rather than plain fetch, so private or rate-limited buckets still resolve
Base64 encoding is chunked at 8192 bytes to avoid blowing the call stack on String.fromCharCode.apply
Calls the OpenAI REST endpoint directly instead of the shared chatCompletion helper, then hand-writes both the success and error usage-log entries
Accepts the legacy documentImageUrl alongside documentFrontUrl so older callers keep working
Model output is stripped of ``` fences before JSON.parse — the strict-JSON instruction is not trusted
Veriff decision webhook: drives identity_verifications, the customer's verification status and the block list
Veriff codes mapped to internal outcomes: 9001 GREEN/verified, 9102 RED/rejected, 9103 RETRY
The session id lives in payload.id for started/submitted events but in payload.verification.id for decisions
Booking-flow verifications start before the customer exists, so a decision with no matching row inserts a temporary record keyed by vendorData
An external_user_id prefixed 'additional_driver_' updates rental_additional_drivers and skips every customer-table side effect — those drivers are not in `customers`
The document number is checked against tenant-scoped blocked_identities and a hit overrides an approved decision into rejected + customer blocked
With no tenant_id on the verification the blocked-identity check is skipped entirely — logged as a warning, but a real bypass
A blocked-identity hit fans out reminder_critical notifications to every admin/head_admin of the tenant
On a terminal decision the document and face images are pulled from Veriff's media API and archived into the customer-documents bucket
Signature verification runs only when VERIFF_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set AND a signature header is present, so unsigned payloads are accepted by default
The document number is mirrored onto customers.license_number so downstream rental checks do not need the verification row
'submitted' and 'started' events are acknowledged without processing results; only a decision changes outcome state

SMS, WhatsApp, voice calls and voicemail all converge on one chat_channels thread keyed by a channel discriminator
The same normalise-then-digit-suffix phone-to-customer resolution is re-implemented inline in four Twilio webhooks
